Semiconductors  
 
 
 HBM lead should continue to pay off; 1c DRAM transition likely landed softly 
 Switch to net cash position slated for the year; NAND getting increasingly competitive 
 Target price set at W280,000; Our Top semiconductor pick 
Initiate coverage with Buy rating and target price of W280,000 
“Invest in good companies ” has long been a popular saying among stock 
investors. SK hynix has proven itself to be a strong company through multiple 
indicators. Given its robust technological edge, we believe the company has 
what it takes to become an even better stock. 
- The early-mover advantage in the HBM market looks poised to continue for 
a while. Underpinned by a solid cost structure, SK hynix stands to be the 
most lucrative business among the three major DRAM players. We think this 
lead will continue to pay off even in the forthcoming HBM4 era. 
- SK hynix also appears to have delivered a soft landing in its transition to the 
1c DRAM node, which will be a key earnings driver over the next two years. 
Despite being in the early stage of operation, production yield is estimated 
to be in the high 80% range. 
- Risks are mitigating. The chip giant is set to shift to a net cash position within 
the year, along with strengthening HBM-led profitability, while NAND is 
getting increasingly competitive. 
While the market continues to apply a conservative valuation to SK hynix given 
its relatively high beta amid prevailing uncertainties, we believe a re-rating will 
follow once the headwinds clouding the cycle begins to lift. We initiate coverage 
with a Buy rating and set our target price at W280,000, applying a target P/B of 
2.0x (past 3yr avg +2std). SK hynix our Top semiconductor pick.

SK hynix (000660) 
 
 
 
2   
  Investment point I. One step ahead in DRAM 
  Good technology creates good products. SK hynix ’s successful ramp -up of 1b DRAM has 
significantly enhanced its HBM3e competitiveness, and helped the company sustain strong 
momentum with its next-generation 1c DRAM node. With its core focus for 2025–2026—HBM and 
1c DRAM—being on track, SK hynix should continue to stand out in DRAM. 
1. HBM lead fuels market dominance 
For the time being, SK Hynix looks likely to continue enjoying its first-mover advantage in the HBM 
market. The company is well-positioned to maintain its competitive edge even into 2026, given its 
outstanding cost structure. While some may argue that this advantage is already priced in, we think 
sustained edge would potentially turn market sentiment around. 
1) HBM3e: Even when prices fall 
HBM3e’s supply-demand dynamics should start improving by 2026 at the latest, as three major 
DRAM suppliers join competition. Also, with HBM3e becoming a legacy product following the onset 
of the HBM4 cycle, HBM3e ASP could come under increased downward pressure. Even if that’s 
the case, SK hynix’s robust cost structure should help the company sustain strong margins even 
amid pricing pressure. 
2) HBM4: First mover, again 
Chances are that the market lead advantage will extend into the HBM4 market. The company is 
reportedly conducting sample testing with its key clients, and a revenue recognition from initial mass 
production is expected in 4Q25. Given its expected lead, SK hynix is poised to maintain a leading 
position even in the early HBM4 market. 
3) Increasing profit contribution 
HBM profit contribution should increase into 2H25. We project revenue growth for HBM to stay 
elevated amid growing shipments and a product mix increasingly skewed toward advanced node-
based products. 
4) What would be the next catalyst? 
Negotiations with major North American clients for 2026 HBM volumes are expected to conclude 
within the first half. If the company succeeds in passing on HBM4 cost increase through pricing, its 
earnings potential will rise further, prompting a positive market response. We view this outcome as 
highly probable. 
2. Seamless transition to 1c DRAM node 
We believe SK hynix has achieved a soft landing in its ramp-up of 1c DRAM, a key driver for the 
next two years. N ew technologies typically begin with a 60–70% yield rate, but SK hynix is 
estimated to have reached mature yield levels in the high 80% range even in the early phase of 
ramp-up. This early stabilization of a new node should provide a meaningful boost to its DRAM 
business competitiveness.

SK hynix (000660) 
 
 
 
4   
  Investment point II. Mitigating risks 
  The risks that once clouded the chipmaker now seem to be lifting amid the company’s continued 
efforts to strengthen its business competitiveness, which we think will serve as a key driver of 
valuation re-rating going forward. 
1. Net cash transition to draw investor focus 
Every leap toward becoming a larger company starts with sufficient cash and cash equivalents. 
Assuming no major downturn in the memory cycle during 2H25, we expect SK hynix to seamlessly 
transition to a net cash position within the year, and stronger financials should help boost investor 
confidence. 
(1) Preparing to compete with China 
The threat of Chinese semiconductor players entering the DRAM market is a critical topic for the 
next three years. While technical hurdles may delay their market penetration for the short run, we 
think it’s not ideal to judge China’s potential based solely on its current technological level, given its 
significant advantages―extensive government support and a large domestic market that accounts 
for more than 30% of global demand. If China makes faster strides in technology, competition will 
somehow intensify, making financial health critical for survival. 
(2) Preparing for future tech shifts 
Technology is much likely to evolve in a way that blurs the lines between memory and logic. As 
DRAM technology advances beyond the 10nm threshold, it will increasingly incorporate elements 
of logic processes, requiring higher R&D/new business spending and capital allocation. 
We think this shift to a net cash position marks a turning point , potentially strengthening the 
company’s readiness for future developments, and the company looks on pace to secure driving 
forces to create a virtuous cycle of reinvestment and innovation by investing in future technologies.

  2. Increasing competitiveness from NAND business 
Market perception of SK hynix-affiliated Solidigm is observed to be  shifting. The company has 
successfully penetrated the QLC market with its floating-gate technology and is leading the high-
capacity eSSD market for AI servers (On Premise AI), enhancing business competit iveness. 
Profitability also seems to be improving on the back of reduced depreciation burdens following more 
conservative capital spending and a product mix increasingly centered on QLC (As of 1Q25, Solidigm 
is estimated to be among the top tier in the industry in terms of profitability.) 
Meanwhile, signs of recovery are also materializing for the in-house NAND business. The company 
now strives hard to improve margin, and with supply restraint in place, we expect inventory levels 
to decline to 5–6 weeks by the end of 2025. With an alleviation of inventory overhang and continued 
efforts to streamline discrete business, we see opportunities for further competitiveness gains. 
 
Fig 8.  NAND OPM by quarter  Fig 9.  NAND OPM by year 
 
 
 
Source: Daishin Securities Research Center  Source: Daishin Securities Research Center 
 
  3. Set to be risk-free from capacity constraints through 2026 
One persistent risk facingSK Hynix’s DRAM business is limited capacity. Around 35–40% of the 
company’s DRAM production comes from its factory  in Wuxi, China, where EUV (Extreme 
Ultraviolet) lithography equipment use is restricted, while available fab space in Korea is running 
short. 
Nevertheless, we believe the risk will remain limited in 2026. Early construction of the M15X fab is 
underway, with completion expected around October–November 2025. Factoring in lead time for 
mass production, wafer output should begin by mid-1H26. At the same time, efforts to optimize 
space at existing facilities should further subdue capacity risks.

6   
  Maintain Buy, with target price of W280,000 
  “Invest in good companies” has long been a popular saying among stock investors. SK hynix has 
proven itself to be a strong company through multiple indicators. Given its robust technological edge, 
we believe the company has what it takes to become an even better stock. 
While the market continues to apply a conservative valuation to SK hynix given its relatively high beta 
amid prevailing uncertainties, we believe a re-rating will follow once the headwinds clouding the cycle 
begins to lift. We initiate coverage with a Buy rating and set our target price at W280,000, applying a 
target P/B of 2.0x (past 3yr avg +2std).
